speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify the infant's specific symptoms: does the stridor occur only when lying down or during feeding, and have you noticed any cyanosis or feeding difficulties? Also, was there any exposure to secondhand smoke at home?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia with associated Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD).

Given the classic inspiratory stridor that worsens with neck flexion and feeding, along with post-prandial vomiting, I am confident in this clinical picture. I will not request further tests as the diagnosis is clear from the history; however, I recommend a trial of thickened feeds and head-of-bed elevation to manage the reflux component.
